title: History 8: Adapters era: LoRA and ControlNet

questions.q: According to the lesson, what is the primary functional difference between LoRA and ControlNet?
options: LoRA changes the spatial structure of the image, while ControlNet changes the style or subject.
LoRA changes what the model generates (style, character, concept), while ControlNet changes how it generates it (spatial structure, pose, edges).
LoRA requires retraining the entire base model, while ControlNet only requires loading a new checkpoint.
LoRA is used for transformer-based models only, while ControlNet is used for UNet-based models only.
questions.answer: LoRA changes what the model generates (style, character, concept), while ControlNet changes how it generates it (spatial structure, pose, edges).
questions.why: The 'Why this matters' section explicitly states: 'LoRA... for changing what the model generates (style, character, concept), and ControlNet for changing how it generates it (spatial structure, pose, edges).'

questions.q: In the context of LoRA, what is the mathematical formula for the effective weight during inference?
questions.why: The 'Under the hood' section defines the effective weight during inference as: 'W_effective = W + α · (A · B)'.

questions.q: Why are 'zero convolutions' used in the ControlNet architecture?
options: To reduce the VRAM usage of the ControlNet branch during inference.
To ensure the base model's pre-trained knowledge is not corrupted by noise from the new, untrained ControlNet branch at the start of training.
To allow the ControlNet to replace the base UNet's encoder layers entirely.
To increase the learning rate of the base model weights during fine-tuning.
questions.answer: To ensure the base model's pre-trained knowledge is not corrupted by noise from the new, untrained ControlNet branch at the start of training.
questions.why: The 'Under the hood' section explains that zero convolutions mean the ControlNet branch has 'no effect' on the base model at the start, ensuring 'the base model's pre-trained knowledge is not corrupted by noise from the new, untrained ControlNet branch.'

questions.q: In the provided lab results, what does the value `max_diff_effective = 0` verify?
options: That the LoRA update has no impact on the final image quality.
That the calculation of W_effective = W + ΔW is numerically exact with no floating-point error.
That the rank of the update matrix is exactly 2.
That the relative error between the original and effective weights is 0%.
questions.answer: That the calculation of W_effective = W + ΔW is numerically exact with no floating-point error.
questions.why: The 'Lab' section breakdown states: 'RESULT max_diff_effective = 0: This verifies that our calculation of W_effective = W + ΔW is numerically exact. There is no floating-point error in the reconstruction.'

questions.q: According to the 'Common mistakes' section, what is a recommended starting range for the rank (r) when training a LoRA?
questions.why: The 'Common mistakes' section advises: 'Start with r=16 or r=32 and measure.'
